reuse.why: The change reuses getApproxNumberThreshold but introduces getScheduleAmount alongside the existing getScheduledAmount and independently implements amount resolution in the API.

duplication.why: Amount resolution remains duplicated between two shared helpers and the API serializer despite consolidating four consumers.

placement.why: Shared schedule policy belongs in shared/schedules.ts, but the API serializer also embeds that policy instead of delegating.

scope.why: All edits concern schedule amount planning, API exposure, or their tests.

maintainability.why: Two similarly named amount helpers and an independent API implementation leave maintainers with multiple definitions to update when the policy changes.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts introduces getScheduleAmount instead of extending getScheduledAmount; server/api-models.ts resolves expectedAmount independently of either helper.

disguised_duplication.where: getScheduleAmount reshapes the existing getScheduledAmount dispatch under a nearly identical name, while scheduleModel.toExternal expresses another amount resolver through null coalescing and nested ternaries.

abstraction_drift.where: The new shared resolver gains amountOp and an isapprox branch, but scheduleModel.toExternal independently implements the earlier range policy; existing getScheduledAmount consumers and budget/schedule-template.ts remain on separate definitions.
